summary: Yoshio Takeuchi worked in sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1907 to 1910 and held a post at Tohoku University from circa 1923 to 1946.

Yoshiro Imaeda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Ariane Macdonald and Rolf Alfred Stein. He worked at CNRS, the National Library of Bhutan, and Kyoto University.

Yoshiro Tamura worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. He earned degrees from the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, and held academic posts at Toyo University, Rissho University, and the University of Tokyo.

Yoshitaka Iriya was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held posts at Kyoto University, Nagoya University, and Kyoto Sangyo University.
Yoshitoyo Ohara works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held appointments at Kyoto University, attested in 2006, and at Kyoto National Museum, attested in 2016.

Yoshitsugu Sawai works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tenri University, Tohoku University, and Harvard University, where his doctoral supervisor was John B. Carman. He held a professorship at Tenri University from circa 1987 to 2017.
Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who held posts at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998–2006) and special appointed full-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe earned his doctorate of science at Tohoku University circa 1966–1975. He held long-term positions at Tohoku University from 1975 to 2012 and in 2018, alongside appointments at UC Berkeley and JAIST.
Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University from circa 1935 to 1939 and later served there as a professor from circa 1958 to 1987.

Youru Wang works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, later serving on the faculty at Rowan University (attested 2003–2007).
Yu Yan Pang is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan.
Yu-Chen Tsui is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed master's studies at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and doctoral studies under Natasha Heller.

Yu-kwan Ng specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and McMaster University under Yün-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara, later holding a post at National Central University.

Yu-min Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Supervised in graduate studies by John C. Huntington, Lee served as a professor at National Taiwan University, attested in 2002.
Yuan Ren is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed a PhD at McMaster University under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff, attested in 1998.
Yuanxing Guo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Gongga Rinpoche. He held posts at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism and the Jinling Scriptural Press.

Yuanying Shi was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under several traditional teachers. He served as abbot at Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples, and was president of the Buddhist Association of China.
Yudru Tsomu specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

Yuen Ren Chao was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Cornell and Harvard universities. His main posts included appointments at Tsinghua University (circa 1925–1929) and the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1947–1963).
Yuexia was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University and served there as a teacher.
